deep.reconstruction: Context (Tractatus de numerorum doctrina, Ch. 11, cubic residues). Let p = 6q+1 be prime. The cubic residues are the nonzero classes congruent to a cube mod p. There are 2q of them: 1, α, β, γ, ... A nonzero class is a residue iff a^{2q} ≡ 1 (mod p). In §§397-399 Euler showed that one non-residue A gives two 'orders' of non-residues: A·R = {A, Aα, Aβ, ...} and A²·R = {A², A²α, ...}, each of size 2q. Modern form: the cubes R form a subgroup of index 3 in (Z/p)^*, and the three cosets are R, AR, A²R. §400 (top of page). Suppose B is a non-residue lying in neither order. Then BR and B²R are further non-residues, each of size 2q, and Euler asserts they are disjoint from the previous classes. [My justification: if B²α = Aβ, then B = B⁴·B^{-3} lies in A²R, since inverses and products of residues are residues. The other cases are similar.] He then claims that exactly one of AB and AB² is a residue. A marginal note says this still has to be proved: 'if AB is a non-residue, it lies in the order of A, B, A² or B², each absurd'. §401. If AB is not a residue, Euler regroups. He takes the enlarged first order AR ∪ BR and the enlarged second order A²R ∪ B²R. He asserts that every element of the first order times every element of the second gives a residue, and different ones for different factors. That would produce more than 2q residues, which is absurd. Hence BR cannot exist, and the non-residues are exactly AR ∪ A²R. [My remark: plain counting already suffices, since 2q + 4q + 4q = 10q > 6q = p−1.] §402. Each residue class has exactly 2q·3 = 6q / 2q = 3 cube roots, i.e. the map x → x³ is 3-to-1. So for any a with p∤a there is b ≢ a (mod p), 0
errors: §401: the argument is incomplete or circular. The claim that every product (first order)×(second order) is a residue uses the multiplication rule of the cosets AR, A²R for the hypothetical extra coset BR, i.e. what is to be proved. The marginal note itself admits that the claim 'not both AB and AB² are non-residues' still needs proof. A simple count (2q+8q > 6q) would have settled §400 directly, given the disjointness Euler states.

§402: tacit hypotheses. These are p∤a, b chosen with b ≢ a (mod p) so that p∤(a−b), and p∤b for passing to aa+3. The identity 4(a²+ab+b²) = (2a+b)²+3b² is used without being stated. None of these affect correctness.
§404: the condition gcd(y,d)=1 (d∤y) is needed and not stated; otherwise d | x³±ay³ says nothing about a.

results.what: The cubic residues mod p=6q+1 form a set of 2q classes closed under multiplication. The non-residues fall into exactly two classes AR, A²R, with products R·I ⊂ I, I·I ⊂ II, I·II ⊂ R.
results.modern_name: Cubes form the index-3 subgroup of the cyclic group (Z/p)^*; the quotient is cyclic of order 3 (cubic residue character)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (Tractatus, c. 1750, publ. 1849) and Gauss (Disquisitiones, 1801) for the general power-residue theory

results.what: Every prime p≡1 (mod 6) divides a²+ab+b², hence a²+3b², x²+3 and 3x²+1. Proof: x→x³ is 3-to-1, so a³≡b³ with a≢b.
results.modern_name: −3 is a quadratic residue mod p≡1 (mod 3), via a primitive cube root of unity; first step of the proof that p=x²+3y²
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (E272 and related work on x²+3y², 1750s-1760s); statement goes back to Fermat

results.what: Complete table of cubic residues and the two non-residue cosets mod 373, halved via ±.
results.modern_name: Table of cubic residue classes / cubic character mod 373
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (this Tractatus); later systematic tables by Jacobi (Canon Arithmeticus 1839) and others

results.what: If d | x³ ± a y³ (or x³ ± a²y³) with d∤y, then a is a cubic residue mod d.
results.modern_name: Trivial criterion for cubic residuacity via divisors of binary cubic forms

deep.surprise_reason: This is the published Tractatus de numerorum doctrina (Opera Postuma I, 1849), well studied (e.g. Lemmermeyer on Euler's cubic residue conjectures). The page contains the elementary coset theory of cubic residues, the standard cube-root-of-unity proof that −3 is a quadratic residue, and a numerical table. All of this is routine and known as Euler's. The notable conjectures (2 is a cubic residue iff p=x²+27y²) are on the next page.
